body.x: The Seoul Business Agency (SBA, President and CEO Hyun Woo Kim) announced that it held the Global Innovation Forum, the largest nation-led global startup ecosystem networking event at CES 2026, on the second day of the exhibition, Wednesday, January 7 (local time), in Las Vegas, the United States.

The event drew strong attention, featuring a more substantial program than in previous years, thanks to cooperation with seven countries leading the global startup ecosystem. It marked the first nation-based startup competition and networking program of its kind at CES.

The Global Innovation Forum began with the goal of using CES, the world’s largest exhibition, to connect startup ecosystems across countries. The event first launched in 2025 under the name “Seoul Innovation Forum,” in cooperation with five national pavilions, and served as the inaugural gathering of Eureka Park participant countries at CES.

Its success stemmed from demonstrating the potential to evolve into a platform for inter-country cooperation by bringing together global national pavilions in one place, beyond individual booth exhibitions, and having representative innovative startups from each country participate in an IR pitching competition. From 2026, the program strengthened its structure to offer CES-participating startups more stable and expanded opportunities for global collaboration, and rebranded the event as the Global Innovation Forum.

body.cap: An overview of the Global Innovation Forum held on Wednesday, January 7, the second day of CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The 2026 Global Innovation Forum took place based on the close collaboration of startup support organizations from seven countries. The hosting organizations—Seoul Business Agency of South Korea, TTA, Switzerland Global Enterprise, Israel Economic and Trade Office, Japan External Trade Organization, Quebec Government Office of Canada, and Business France—combined their capabilities to ensure the event’s success.

The forum opened with an IR pitching competition featuring startups selected by each participating country. Following the same format as last year, which received a positive response, each country selected outstanding startups to deliver IR pitches to judges and attendees at the forum.

Building on last year’s judging process, which was limited to global media, this year’s competition expanded the judging panel to include representatives from global media outlets and venture capital firms, thereby enhancing investment opportunities for participating companies and strengthening the competition’s credibility. Companies evaluated the forum positively, noting that it allowed them to present their technologies directly to venture capitalists to pursue investment opportunities while simultaneously promoting their products and technologies to global media.

Twenty global media representatives and six venture capital professionals served as judges in the IR pitching competition, evaluating advanced technologies and startup visions from the seven countries based on criteria such as investment attractiveness and global publicity potential.

body.cap: Fasthabit posed with SBA President Hyun Woo Kim for a commemorative photo at the Global Innovation Forum IR pitching competition held on Wednesday, January 7. | Provided by the Seoul Business Agency

body.x: As a result of the competition, the Grand Award was presented to Firsthabit from South Korea’s Seoul Pavilion, the Scale-up Award went to Hua Tech International from TTA, and the Impact Award was awarded to CubicSpace from the Quebec Government Office of Canada. Each winner received a trophy along with prize money of USD 3,000, USD 2,000, and USD 1,000, respectively.

Firsthabit, the Seoul Pavilion company that won first place, said, “We did not expect to win, so this feels like a great reward for all the hard work we have put in. Starting with CES 2026 and this Global Innovation Forum award, we plan to seriously pursue entry into the U.S. market,” sharing its acceptance remarks.

Participating startups that did not receive awards also expressed positive feedback, saying, “The Global Innovation Forum was a place where startups with diverse cultural and technological backgrounds gathered to share insights and strengthen their determination to open global markets.”

In the panel discussion that followed, representatives from participating countries introduced their respective startup support programs and discussed key agendas for the global startup ecosystem. The session provided a meaningful opportunity to share the know-how of institutions that have led the global startup ecosystem by showcasing innovative startups at CES year after year.

body.cap: A panel discussion takes place at the Global Innovation Forum. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The significantly enhanced networking session was another highlight of the event. Beyond the judges, a wide range of stakeholders from the startup ecosystem—including global venture capitalists, media representatives, startups, and startup support organizations from various countries—participated, creating a vibrant atmosphere of exchange and underscoring the forum’s status as the largest global networking event at CES.

During the networking session following the competition, participants freely exchanged views on major issues and insights in the tech industry. Startups visiting the event welcomed the opportunity to connect with key players in the startup ecosystem and expressed their intention to actively leverage the networks formed to pursue investment and establish footholds for global market entry. The moment underscored the forum’s meaningful contribution to enhancing startups’ CES participation outcomes.

In addition, startups that wished to do so were given the opportunity to take the stage for a one-minute PR speech to promote their technologies, a feature that received high praise for effectively showcasing innovative solutions to stakeholders across the startup ecosystem.

SBA President and CEO Hyun Woo Kim said, “I hope the Global Innovation Forum will establish itself as a symbolic program representing inter-country cooperation and global startup exchange within CES,” adding, “We will continue to develop it so that it becomes the most closely watched event by all players in the global startup ecosystem visiting CES, including media, venture capitalists, startups, and national pavilion representatives.”
